intro: This page is the board and toolchain matrix. It is taken from `config/core-recipes.toml`, `config/core-library.toml`, `profiles/native-integration-dev.toml`, the per-core `toolchain.lock` files, the misteross producers, and the docs those files point at. A cell that is not in those sources is marked unverified or TBD.

The bootstrap image installs `fes.menu` and the pinned splash bitstream. Every playable core is a catalog install. Library standing `supported` is not a claim that the current bitstream has kit acceptance. Dated notes under `docs/validation/` accept only the artifact they name.

Tiers are derived from the tier role, owned RTL dates and media generation; kit notes are recorded but do not set a tier. Catalog standing is stored on each row as a weak signal and is not an input. As of 2026-10-29. The recent cutoff is 2026-10-16. The window starts 2026-08-30. A tier_override with reason Deano 2026-10-29 replaces the derived tier.

tiers.label: Firmware
tiers.meaning: Boot package or pinned idle RBF.

tiers.label: Current
tiers.meaning: Owned RTL on or after 2026-10-16, and media is not the old generation.

tiers.label: Aging
tiers.meaning: Owned RTL in the 60-day window, before 2026-10-16.

tiers.label: Stale
tiers.meaning: No owned RTL in the 60-day window.

tiers.label: Bring-up
tiers.meaning: No recipe. Diagnostic RTL or host simulation in progress.

tiers.label: Bring-up (queued)
tiers.meaning: No package yet. Queued by Deano 2026-10-29.

tiers.label: Shared
tiers.meaning: CPU RTL used by other cores. Not a system package.

tiers.label: Demo
tiers.meaning: Registered demo package, not a machine.

policy: Labels follow the accepted Quartus policy in [Quartus-built cores](design/quartus-cores.md) (issue #1163). `oss` is the Debian-style main set: Yosys + nextpnr-mistral. `quartus` is the non-free set: a proprietary toolchain. A core build is supposed to say which one made it, so an all-OSS selection can exclude every Quartus build. `FES_OSS_ONLY` is not implemented. Current registered recipes and package selection build the OSS lane only. A failed OSS route never falls back to Quartus.

Both labelled builds ship only when the published rule is met, on the same RTL and the same target clocks. Either every Quartus sign-off seed closes a required clock that an OSS sign-off seed misses, or the best complete-seed Fmax is at least 15% higher on any required clock: `100 × (Quartus best − OSS best) / OSS best`. Otherwise the core ships OSS only. No registered recipe declares a `toolchains` list yet, so no core ships both builds today. The i386 far-transfer numbers (about 40%) remain the worked example of a gap large enough for that rule. i386, pc386 and PC/XT are separately Quartus-primary; their nextpnr builds are advisory.

DE25-Nano (Agilex 5) is Quartus-only (policy); shell pending. policy: Deano 2026-10-29. Rows with a DE10 board bitstream show Quartus; rows without a board bitstream show no DE25 toolchain cell. Agilex 5 has no OSS reverse-engineering, so there is no OSS toolchain for that device. nextpnr-mistral targets Cyclone V (`5CSEBA6U23I7` in [the DE10-Nano board note](../sources/misteross/boards/de10nano/README.md)). Quartus Pro 24.1 or later is the first release that supports Agilex 5 ([Quartus-built cores](design/quartus-cores.md)). `sources/misteross/boards/de25nano` may be absent or present; the checker treats that landing as expected. Per-core DE25 cells stay on the policy line until the shell is on this branch and those cells are re-verified.

i386, pc386 and PC/XT use Quartus (primary, policy). policy: Deano 2026-10-29. nextpnr builds are advisory, and a nextpnr miss there is filed as a nextpnr issue, not a blocker. PC/XT has a registered Quartus diagnostic package producer and an advisory nextpnr diagnostic. pc386 retains pack-only nextpnr synthesis, and i386 retains the Quartus 17.0.2 fit of its Yosys netlist ([i386 CPU design](../sources/misteross/docs/i386-cpu-design.md), DeanoC/nextpnr#300). Those tree facts do not change the primary label.

ColecoVision still uses the old media handling. Its example arcade room has an empty-library status when no matching titles are available. Updating that handling is low priority and is folded into the wider Coleco work (for example Adam support). policy: Deano 2026-10-29. The checked-in factory recipe is the format-4 ROM map, and it strips the blob and blob-stream mailboxes that the older Coleco producers still declare.

Input: `fes.gamepad.ports` and `fes.keypad.ports`. HDMI: native-pixel shell, mandatory Direct or Scanlines part, then the session display plane, fixed 720p60. CPU: TV80, not `fes_z80_nmos`. Updating it is low priority and is folded into the wider Coleco work (for example Adam support). The `example.coleco-arcade` room names five cabinets and lists only those with matching titles; its empty-library status says `no Coleco arcade titles in this library yet` only when none match. Older `build_fes_coleco.py` and `build_fes_coleco_oss.py` still declare blob and blob-stream; they are not the recipe producer. Deano 2026-10-29: the tier is Aging. Work toward Current is in progress and still needs work (media handling and the wider Coleco work).

cores.label: `fes_i386_cpu`
cores.router: CPU timing spikes use this lock with the GPU router. Not a package producer and not a recipe row.
cores.quartus: Quartus (primary, policy). policy: Deano 2026-10-29. nextpnr builds are advisory, and a nextpnr miss is filed as a nextpnr issue, not a blocker. Quartus 17.0.2 fits the same Yosys netlist (`scripts/quartus_fes_i386.py`). The far-transfer record is about 69–74 MHz nextpnr and about 98–104 MHz Quartus. A nextpnr-only gap is filed on the flow (DeanoC/nextpnr#300, `docs/i386-cpu-design.md`). Recipe and package selection for a labelled variant are not implemented.
cores.features: Not a system package. No media, HDMI, Bluetooth or mesh of its own. Phase 1 real-mode pipeline is in progress in the CPU design doc. The pc386 machine is its consumer: the development package `fes.pc386` (pc386 M5) seals it with Quartus 17.0.2.
cores.notes: Shared CPU RTL. Device `5CSEBA6U23I7` in the spike harness. Yosys pin `238eac9a` is newer than the repository lock's `3a5accbd` and is scoped to this CPU.

Launch, library and mesh are host services. No per-core mesh capability flag was found, so this page does not claim that any core is in or out of the mesh.

No recipe records a completed OSS-versus-Quartus sign-off comparison against the 15% rule. i386 is the worked example of the gap and is Quartus-primary by policy; it is not a registered core. Which other current cores would qualify to ship a Quartus variant is unverified.

Core status and the validation notes bind acceptance to named packages. This matrix does not copy those package ids forward. Which rows Deano wants marked HIL-verified for the bytes in the tree is open.

tier_rules: As of 2026-10-29. Window 2026-08-30 through that day. Recent cutoff 2026-10-16.

Owned RTL: a commit that changes that core's rtl/ and whose subject names the core, or where that core holds at least half of the commit's RTL paths and at least two files. A one-file edit inside another core's commit is not owned RTL.
Catalog standing is recorded and is not read by the tier rule.
firmware, shared, demo, reference and bring-up come from tier_role, not from dates.
Otherwise a play row is current when owned RTL is on or after the cutoff, aging when owned RTL is in the window before the cutoff, and stale when it has none.
last_hil_pass is a designated-kit note. It does not by itself set the tier. A host seal or a simulation PASS is not a kit pass.
A play row with media_gen old and owned RTL on or after the recent cutoff derives to unresolved. That result is not a displayed tier. A tier_override with reason Deano 2026-10-29 replaces it.
Coleco derives to unresolved and is Aging by that override. Work toward Current is in progress and still needs work (media handling and the wider Coleco work).
Spectrum and Atari ST derive to current. The same override confirms that tier. Their kit HIL pass on the latest RTL is pending and expected soon.
C64 NTSC and Atari STE have no package. Their override tier is bring-up-queued.
Spectrum +2 is a ROM variant of fes.spectrum128 (kind rom). It is the same core and the same model, with a different ROM. Deano 2026-10-29.
needs_deano: SMS and SG-1000 catalog standing is supported. Tier aging uses owned RTL on 2026-10-06 and kit diagnostics on 2026-09-29. The catalog flag was not used.
Pong catalog standing is supported. No owned RTL in the 60-day window, so the tier is stale. The catalog flag was not used.
ZX80, TS1000 and TS1500 share the ZX81 shell. Kit notes name fes.zx81 (2026-10-22), not those three. The 2026-10-25 model commit is after that note.
Apple II kit diagnostic is 2026-09-27. Owned RTL is 2026-10-06 (#549). No later kit note was found.
Open issues on each row are title matches, not a full blocker audit.
